title: A log reader that outgrows its read-everything design

initial_repo.README.md:
# events

Log file reader. See git history for the design conversation.

stages.message: events.py: read_events(path) reads our log files — one event per line, formatted 'LEVEL|message' — and returns a list of dicts with 'level' and 'message'. Write tests.

requirements.text: read_events(path) parses 'LEVEL|message' lines into a list of {'level', 'message'} dicts

stages.message: Log files got huge and we usually only want the first few events. Can we get iterate(source) that yields events one at a time instead of building the whole list? It should also take an already-open file, the uploader hands us those. read_events can stay as it is.

requirements.text: iterate(source) yields parsed events lazily, accepts a path or an open file object; read_events keeps working

stages.message: One more thing: a level filter on iterate, like iterate(source, level='ERROR'). Still one at a time — we stop reading the file as soon as we've got what we need.

requirements.text: iterate(source, level=...) filters by level without reading ahead
